original_query: retrocompact open subset U of X
original_context: Topology: retrocompact open subset U of X, whose intersections with each quasi-compact open subset V⊆X are quasi-compact; not equivalent to U itself being quasi-compact in arbitrary X.
definition: Let X be a topological space. An open subset U⊆X is retrocompact in X if, for every quasi-compact open V⊆X, the intersection U∩V is quasi-compact. Equivalently, the inclusion U↪X is a quasi-compact map.
reasoning: This is a named, precisely typed property of an open subset relative to its ambient space, specializing the existing independently screened quasi-compact map meaning to an inclusion. It is not the same as requiring U itself be quasi-compact without assuming X quasi-compact. The existing constructible-subset meaning uses retrocompact opens as prerequisites, and neither that construction nor the general quasi-compact-space meaning is synonymous with this named subset property. Preserve it as a specialization/contextual entry rather than force an equivalence alias.

sources.relevance: Directly checked primary source: quasi-compact map tests preimages of quasi-compact opens, and a subset is retrocompact exactly when its inclusion is quasi-compact; this gives the intersection formulation.
